name: Walters v. National Association of Radiation Survivors
summary: The Supreme Court upheld a $10 cap on attorney fees for representation before the VA, finding it did not violate due process because veterans had sufficient access to non-attorney representatives and the system was designed to be non-adversarial.
significance: The central precedent directly at issue — the Court previously upheld a $10 fee cap on attorney compensation in veterans benefits cases, and Johnson argues that precedent should be reconsidered or distinguished given changes in the law and the complexity of modern VA proceedings.
